'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]
**[[Makugwe massacre]]
***[[Allied Democratic Forces]] [[insurgent]]s kill 23 people at a [[Bar (establishment)|bar]] in [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. The [[jihadism|jihadists]] also torched several homes and shops in the village during the attack. [[Islamic State]] claims responsibility. [https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20230123-islamic-state-group-claims-deadly-attack-in-east-dr-congo (AFP via France 24)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2021–2023 inflation surge]]
**Swedish [[music streaming service]] [[Spotify]] announces that it will cut 600 jobs, around 6% of its workforce, citing low revenue growth and a need to improve efficiency. [[Dawn Ostroff]] will also depart as its chief content and advertising business officer. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-64374583 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A major [[power outage]] in [[Pakistan]] leaves nearly 220 million people without electricity after a failure at the national [[power grid]]. Earlier this month, [[Prime Minister of Pakistan|Prime Minister]] [[Shehbaz Sharif]] ordered a reduction in energy consumption as the country faces a severe energy crisis. [https://edition.cnn.com/2023/01/22/asia/pakistan-power-outage-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/pakistan-suffers-major-power-outage-after-grid-failure-2023-01-23/ (Reuters)]
*An [[Algerian Air Force]] [[Mil Mi-17#Export_variants|Mi-171]] helicopter crashes during a [[military exercise]], killing three crew onboard in [[Aïn Defla Province]], [[Algeria]]. [https://en.mehrnews.com/news/196557/3-killed-in-military-helicopter-crash-in-Algeria (MEHR)]
*Two people are killed and two others are injured after a fire in a church in [[Beyoğlu]], [[Istanbul]], [[Turkey]]. [https://www.dailysabah.com/turkey/istanbul/2-die-2-injured-after-fire-at-armenian-catholic-church-in-istanbul (DailySabah)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Sweden–Turkey relations]]
**[[Enlargement of NATO]], [[Sweden–NATO relations]]
***[[President of Turkey|Turkish President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] rules out Turkish support for Sweden's bid for [[NATO]] membership following the [[Quran desecration|burning]] of a [[Quran]] outside the Turkish embassy in [[Stockholm]] by [[Rasmus Paludan]] and a series of pro-Kurdish demonstrations where protestors waved [[PKK]] flags. [https://apnews.com/article/nato-politics-turkey-government-recep-tayyip-erdogan-f9a568da05914a4143a033e74067b6f4 (AP)]
*[[Estonia–Russia relations]]
**[[Estonia]] announces the expulsion of the [[List of ambassadors of Russia to Estonia|Russian ambassador]] in [[Embassy of Russia, Tallinn|Tallinn]] {{interlanguage link|Vladimir Lipayev|ru|Липаев, Владимир Георгиевич}} to [[Reciprocity (international relations)|reciprocate]] Russia's expulsion of the [[List of ambassadors of Estonia to Russia|Estonian ambassador]] in [[Embassy of Estonia, Moscow|Moscow]] [[Margus Laidre]] due to a "downgrade" of relations. Both envoys will depart their respective assignments on February 7. [https://apnews.com/article/estonia-tallinn-business-67182f99b4eaae30d1fd41d12da8fa48 (AP)]
*[[Latvia–Russia relations]]
**[[Latvia]] asks [[List of ambassadors of Russia to Latvia|Russian ambassador]] {{interlanguage link|Mikhail Vanin|ru|Ванин, Михаил Валентинович}} to leave the country by February 24 in "full solidarity" with Estonia. [https://www.politico.eu/article/estonia-latvia-russia-remove-european-union-tensions-moscow/ (Politico)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Mass shootings in the United States]]
**[[2023 Monterey Park shooting]]
***An eleventh person dies in the hospital from injuries sustained in Saturday's [[mass shooting]] in [[Monterey Park, California]], United States. [https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2023-01-23/victims-identified-in-the-monterey-park-shooting (''Los Angeles Times'')]
**[[2023 Half Moon Bay shootings]]
***Seven people are killed and one other person is injured in a [[shooting spree]] in [[Half Moon Bay, California]], United States. A suspect is taken into custody afterwards. [https://www.sfchronicle.com/bayarea/article/Sheriff-deputies-in-Half-Moon-Bay-responding-to-17737044.php (''San Francisco Chronicle'')]
*Aftermath of the [[2020 Beirut explosion]]
**Judge [[Tarek Bitar]] resumes his investigation into the [[explosion]], 13 months after [[Hezbollah]] officials filed complaints against Bitar that prompted him to suspend the investigation. [https://www.zawya.com/en/world/middle-east/lebanon-port-blast-probe-resumes-after-13-months-halt-judicial-source-ttbprai2 (AFP via Zawya)]
*[[Eugenics in Japan]]
**The {{interlanguage link|Kumamoto district court|ja|熊本地方裁判所}} orders the [[Government of Japan|government]] to [[Financial compensation|compensate]] two [[plaintiff]]s {{¥|22 million|link=yes}} ([[United States dollar|US$]]170,000) worth of [[damages]] for their [[compulsory sterilization]] under the now-[[Desuetude|obsolete]] [[Eugenic Protection Act of 1948]]. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2023/01/0bccfc853dde-update1-japan-court-orders-govt-to-pay-damages-over-forced-sterilization.html (Kyodo News)]
